tools.name: pipe__get
tools.description: Read the arguments or the result of an earlier tool call by its handle. Handle forms: "c3.out" (result), "c3.in" (arguments); add a path to read part of a value, e.g. "c3.out.items[0].id". Optional "jq" applies a jq filter to the value first. "status" returns the connected servers and any startup errors.

handle.description: call handle with optional path, or "status"

jq.description: optional jq filter applied to the value

tools.name: pipe__patch
tools.description: Re-run an earlier tool call with modified arguments. Use it whenever a call needs to be repeated with a change — it failed, or you want a different filter, column, limit or target — instead of writing the whole call again: you send only the change, and the arguments stay exactly as they were everywhere else. The call's stored arguments are copied, the edits are applied to the copy, and the result is executed as a new call with its own handle. Edit forms: {find, replace} replaces text in string arguments (all of them, or only under "path"); {path, set} sets the value at "path". With no edits the call is re-run unchanged. To fix a step of a run instead, pass "run" (run id) and "step": the edits apply to the step definition (e.g. path "args.sql", or find/replace in its text) and the run continues from that step; earlier steps are not repeated.

run.description: run id (with "step"); or, with "call", false to only store the new call

path.description: path inside the arguments / step, e.g. "a.b[0]"

rerun.description: with run+step: continue the run after patching (default true)

tools.name: pipe__transform
tools.description: Reshape a stored value with a jq filter and store the output under a new handle, without the data passing through the conversation. "from" is a handle with optional path (e.g. "c3.out.items").

from.description: handle of the input value, e.g. "c3.out"

tools.name: pipe__map
tools.description: Call one tool once per item of a stored list, in a single request. "over" is a handle of a list (e.g. "c3.out.rows", or "{{ c3.out | map(.id) }}"). In "args", "{{ item }}" is the current item and "{{ item.<path> }}" part of it. Returns how many calls succeeded, the failures, and a handle per call; the outputs are stored as a list under the map's own handle. "dry_run" returns the plan only.

over.description: handle of the list to iterate

args.description: arguments for each call; may use {{ item }} refs

confirm.description: only if a reply asked for it: the token from that needs_confirm reply

tools.name: pipe__run
tools.description: Run a multi-step plan in one request: pass a new "chain" (JSON or YAML text, e.g. copied from a skill) with its "params", or an existing "run" id to run it again. Use it as soon as you know the remaining steps — typically after a few single calls to look at the inputs — and especially when one step's result feeds the next: the steps run back to back without a round trip to you, intermediate results stay stored instead of passing through the conversation, and a failed step is fixed in place. A chain is {params?: {name: type}, steps: [...]}; each step has an "id" and one of: {call: "<tool>", args: {...}} calls a tool; {jq: "<program>"} computes a value, with params and earlier step outputs as jq variables ($id); {map: "<tool>", over: "<step id or handle of a list>", args: {...}} calls a tool once per item ("{{ item }}", "{{ item.path }}"); {ai: "<task>", input?: "<jq program>", by?: "session"|"subagent", batch?: n, expect?: <JSON Schema>} pauses the run for a step that needs judgement (done by you or a subagent), continued with pipe__resume. In args, "{{ name[.path] [| jq] }}" refers to a param, an earlier step's output, or any handle. The reply lists each step's output handle and the last step's result. A failing step stops the run; fix it with pipe__patch {run, step, edits}, which re-runs from that step without repeating earlier ones. "from" re-runs from a step; "dry_run" returns the plan; "force" repeats map items that already succeeded.

from.description: step id to run again from

dry_run.description: validate and return the plan without running it

confirm.description: only if a reply asked for it: the token from that needs_confirm reply

tools.name: pipe__resume
tools.description: Give the result of a paused ai step and continue its run. "output" is checked against the step's "expect"; if it does not match, the reply says why and the run stays paused. For a batched step, resume each chunk by its index.

WITH u AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(signup_date) sd FROM users_data GROUP BY user_id HAVING sd BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
a AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.user_id, CAST(julianday(date(d.event_time)) - julianday(u.sd) AS INT) dn FROM users_data d JOIN u USING(user_id)),
r AS (SELECT u.user_id, strftime('%Y-%m', u.sd) cohort,

content.text:
I worked out retention for last quarter, put the numbers in a new spreadsheet, and posted a summary with the link to #analytics.

**What I measured:** Today is 2026‑11‑12, so "last quarter" is Q3 2026. That's the 354 users who signed up between Jul 1 and Sep 30. A user counts as retained if they did anything (login, page view or purchase) during the window:
- **D1:** the day after signup
- **D7:** days 7–13 after signup
- **D30:** days 30–36 after signup

The data runs to 2026‑11‑11, so the D30 window is complete for every Q3 signup.

| Signup month | Users | D1 | D7 | D30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2026 | 121 | 31.4% | 67.8% | 48.8% |
| Aug 2026 | 118 | 30.5% | 65.3% | 51.7% |
| Sep 2026 | 115 | 37.4% | 61.7% | 45.2% |
| **Q3 total** | **354** | **33.1%** | **65.0%** | **48.6%** |

September's signups had the best D1 but the weakest D7 and D30.

D7 is higher than D1 because D1 covers a single day while D7 covers seven. If you'd rather use different windows, or count a user as retained if they're active on day N or any time after, I can rerun it.

The table's description says the user column is `usr_id`, but it's actually `user_id`. Someone may want to fix the description.

**Spreadsheet:** https://sheets.example.com/sh1
